title: Australia PM Criticized for Sexist Remarks About Japanese Melon Gifts
content:
Former Japanese Ambassador to South Korea, Masahiro Tanaka, condemned remarks made by a South‑Korean lawmaker that he described as “sexist” and said they “betrayed the close bond” between the two countries. The comments, which surfaced in a parliamentary debate last week, targeted Japanese women and were widely criticized by Japanese officials and civil‑society groups.

Tanaka, speaking at a Tokyo press conference, urged both governments to address the issue and to reinforce the diplomatic and economic partnership that has expanded over the past decade. He added that such remarks undermine the trust built through joint initiatives on trade, security and cultural exchange. The South‑Korean lawmaker’s party has yet to issue a formal apology, and the incident has prompted calls for clearer guidelines on respectful discourse in bilateral forums.
author: BBC World

title: Libyan authorities fight fire after third drone strike on Zawiya refinery
content:
The Zawiya refinery in Libya was hit by a drone strike on Monday, marking the third attack on the facility in just two days. The strike, reported by local authorities, caused significant damage to the refinery’s infrastructure, though no casualties were confirmed at the time of the report. The refinery, one of the country’s largest oil processing plants, has been a frequent target amid the ongoing security crisis in the region.

Earlier incidents on Saturday and Sunday involved similar drone assaults that disrupted operations and damaged storage tanks. Libyan officials have condemned the attacks and urged international partners to support efforts to secure critical infrastructure. The repeated strikes underscore the vulnerability of key energy assets in the conflict zone and raise concerns about the stability of the country’s oil supply chain.

Authorities are investigating the drone operators and assessing the full extent of the damage. The refinery’s management has announced plans to resume limited operations pending repairs. The series of attacks highlights the persistent threat to Libya’s energy sector and the broader implications for regional energy markets.
author: BBC World

title: Syrian former president Bashar al-Assad sentenced to death in absentia
content:
An international tribunal has found the former head of state guilty of war crimes and crimes against humanity committed during the nation’s protracted civil war. The verdict, delivered after a lengthy trial that examined evidence of systematic attacks on civilian populations, confirmed that the ex‑president orchestrated and authorized widespread atrocities, including mass killings, forced displacement, and the deliberate targeting of humanitarian aid workers.

The conviction, which carries a substantial prison sentence, marks a landmark moment for accountability in the region and underscores the international community’s commitment to prosecuting senior officials for violations of humanitarian law. Officials from the court emphasized that the judgment aims to provide justice for victims and to deter future abuses, while the former president’s legal team has announced plans to appeal the decision.
author: BBC World

title: Zelensky says Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia used North Korean missiles
content:
Kyiv’s president announced that a recent strike on the city of Zaporizhzhia resulted in at least six fatalities and 19 injuries, attributing the attack to ballistic missiles supplied by a Russian ally. The missiles hit residential areas in the southern Ukrainian region, prompting emergency services to conduct rescue operations and medical teams to treat the wounded.

Ukrainian officials said the weapons used were identified as a type commonly exported by the ally, which has previously been implicated in similar attacks across the front line. The incident adds to a series of recent bombardments that have intensified amid ongoing hostilities, and authorities are calling for a thorough investigation to hold the perpetrators accountable under international law.
author: BBC World

title: Trump transferred from Air Force One to military plane after NATO summit in Turkey
content:
Washington, D.C., officials confirmed that the president transferred from the aging Air Force One aircraft to a separate military transport plane while departing the NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey, last month, according to U.S. media reports. The change occurred after the multilateral meeting concluded, with the president boarding a U.S. Air Force C‑17 Globemaster II that was positioned on the tarmac to ferry him back to the United States. The older Boeing 747‑based Air Force One, designated VC‑25A, had been used for the majority of the president’s overseas travel since its introduction in the late 1990s, but logistical considerations at the Turkish airfield prompted the switch.

The move underscores ongoing efforts to modernize the presidential fleet, as the Department of Defense prepares the next‑generation VC‑25B to replace the current aircraft later this decade. While the president’s itinerary remained unchanged, the temporary use of a cargo‑type military plane ensured continuity of secure transport without delay. No further operational issues were reported, and the president’s return proceeded as scheduled.
author: BBC World

title: WNBA Player Sophie Cunningham's Alleged White Privilege Sparks Debate
content:
WNBA Players Speak Out on Racial Disparities in Treatment

A recent controversy has emerged in the WNBA, with a high-profile player alleging that she receives preferential treatment due to her race. The claim, made by a WNBA rival of the Indiana Fever's guard, suggests that she is treated differently from her Black peers. This assertion is not without basis, as evidence has shown that racial disparities in treatment are a persistent issue in various professional sports leagues. The phenomenon of white privilege, a concept that acknowledges the unearned advantages and benefits that white individuals receive in a society with a history of systemic racism, has been a long-standing topic of discussion.

The situation involving DiJonai Carrington and Sophie Cunningham has brought renewed attention to the issue of racial disparities in the WNBA. While some may dismiss the claim as an overreaction or a personal attack, the reality is that there are numerous examples of white players receiving more favorable treatment and opportunities than their Black counterparts. The WNBA, like many other professional sports leagues, has a long history of racial disparities in treatment, from hiring practices to playing time and media coverage. By acknowledging and addressing these issues, the league can work towards creating a more equitable and inclusive environment for all players.

The WNBA's response to this controversy will be closely watched, as the league seeks to maintain its reputation as a leader in promoting diversity and inclusion. By taking concrete steps to address racial disparities in treatment, the WNBA can demonstrate its commitment to creating a more just and equitable environment for all players, regardless of their race or background.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ancient Colombian Communities Built Large Cooperative Water System, Study Finds
content:
Archaeologists have uncovered evidence that thousands of years ago, Colombian communities constructed a sophisticated irrigation and water‑storage system through cooperative efforts among family groups, without any centralized authority. The new study, published in the *Journal of Andean Archaeology*, details how these early societies engineered terraces, canals, and reservoirs that regulated water flow across the highlands, enabling sustained agriculture in a region prone to seasonal droughts.

The research team argues that the same principles of decentralized, community‑driven planning could inform modern policy responses to Colombia’s escalating water‑management crisis. By drawing on local knowledge and fostering collaboration among municipalities, regional planners could replicate the resilience seen in the ancient system, potentially reducing dependence on costly, top‑down infrastructure projects. The study’s authors caution that any contemporary application must be tailored to current environmental and socio‑economic conditions, but emphasize that the historical precedent demonstrates the viability of grassroots engineering solutions.

In light of these findings, Colombian policymakers are urged to reassess current water‑management strategies, prioritizing participatory approaches that engage local stakeholders. If adopted, such a shift could enhance adaptive capacity, improve resource distribution, and provide a more sustainable framework for addressing the country’s water challenges.
author: Phys.org

title: Standard Model of Physics Under Review
content: The Standard Model of particle physics stands as one of the most rigorously tested and successful frameworks in modern science, yet its comprehensive structure is now facing renewed scrutiny. In a recent column, physicist and writer Chanda Prescod-Weinstein examines whether the theory’s extensive catalog of particles and forces contains unnecessary components. As experimental results continue to challenge certain predictions, the scientific community is increasingly questioning whether the model’s current architecture is essential or if it carries theoretical excess
author: New Scientist

title: Decline in Reading Habits Raises Concerns
content:
Despite the growing popularity of books, research suggests that people are reading less frequently due to the increasing number of distractions competing for their attention. This trend is concerning because reading has numerous cognitive benefits that are being overlooked as a result. The decline in literacy rates can have far-reaching consequences, affecting various aspects of cognitive function, including memory and intelligence quotient (IQ). To better understand the implications of this trend, experts in the field of psychology and science are weighing in on the importance of reading and its impact on cognitive development.

According to experts such as Prof Falk Huettig, an experimental psychologist at the Max Planck Institute for Psycholinguistics, and Ian Sample, the Guardian's science editor, the benefits of reading are multifaceted. They have discussed the topic in-depth, exploring the ways in which reading can improve cognitive function and mitigate the risks associated with declining literacy rates. Prof Huettig, author of The Perks of Being a Bookworm, has conducted extensive research on the subject, providing valuable insights into the importance of reading for maintaining and improving cognitive abilities. By examining the latest research and findings, it becomes clear that reading plays a vital role in supporting overall cognitive health.

In conclusion, the decline in reading habits is a pressing concern that can have significant consequences for cognitive function and overall well-being. As experts continue to highlight the importance of reading, it is essential to recognize the value of this activity and make a concerted effort to prioritize it in our increasingly busy lives. By doing so, we can reap the numerous benefits of reading and mitigate the risks associated with declining literacy rates, ultimately supporting healthier and more resilient cognitive function.
author: Guardian Science

title: Total Solar Eclipse to Occur Over Europe
content:
A rare celestial event is set to occur on Wednesday, 12 August, as the Moon passes directly between the Earth and the Sun, resulting in a solar eclipse. This phenomenon will be visible to millions of people across Europe, with a wide band of north and central Spain, as well as parts of Portugal, Greenland, and Iceland, experiencing a total eclipse. The path of totality will be limited to these specific regions, where the light of the setting sun will be almost completely obscured.

In addition to the areas experiencing a total eclipse, a larger portion of western Europe will witness a partial eclipse, with the UK, France, Belgium, Switzerland, and northern Italy all being affected. The eclipse will occur in the evening, with the Moon blocking a significant portion of the Sun's light, creating an otherworldly atmosphere. This event is a rare opportunity for people to witness a solar eclipse, and many are expected to gather in the affected areas to observe the phenomenon. The eclipse is a significant astronomical event, and its occurrence is a reminder of the awe-inspiring beauty of the celestial world.

The solar eclipse on 12 August is a unique event that will provide a thrilling experience for those who witness it. As the Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun, it will create a rare and fleeting moment of celestial alignment, allowing people to appreciate the beauty and complexity of the universe. With many Europeans set to witness this event, it is likely to be a memorable experience for those who observe it, and a reminder of the wonders that can be seen in the night sky.
author: Guardian Science

title: Schizophrenia Genetic Architecture Mapped
content:
A significant breakthrough has been made in the field of psychiatric research, as recent findings have shed new light on the genetic architecture of schizophrenia. This complex mental health disorder has long been the subject of intense study, with scientists seeking to understand the underlying genetic mechanisms that contribute to its development. The latest discoveries have provided one of the most detailed pictures to date of the genetic factors involved in schizophrenia, offering a wealth of new information for researchers to explore.

The new findings have been made possible by advances in genetic sequencing technology and the analysis of large datasets. By examining the genetic codes of thousands of individuals with schizophrenia, researchers have been able to identify specific genetic variants that are associated with an increased risk of developing the disorder. This has enabled scientists to build a more comprehensive understanding of the genetic architecture of schizophrenia, including the identification of specific genes and biological pathways that are involved. The insights gained from this research have the potential to inform the development of new treatments and therapies for schizophrenia, and may ultimately lead to improved outcomes for individuals affected by the disorder.

The implications of these findings are significant, as they open up new avenues for research into the causes and consequences of schizophrenia. By continuing to explore the genetic architecture of the disorder, scientists may be able to identify new targets for intervention and develop more effective strategies for prevention and treatment. As research in this area continues to evolve, it is likely that our understanding of schizophrenia will become increasingly sophisticated, ultimately leading to better care and support for those affected by this complex and debilitating condition.
author: Wired

title: Turkey Approves Conditional Pardon Bill for Thousands of PKK Militants
content:
Turkey’s parliament approved a new law on Monday that would grant conditional pardons to thousands of Kurdish militants, a move aimed at advancing the government’s stalled peace initiative with the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK). The legislation, which passed with a majority vote, allows eligible fighters to receive amnesty in exchange for surrendering weapons and renouncing violence. The Turkish government has framed the measure as a necessary step toward ending decades of armed conflict and restoring stability in the predominantly Kurdish southeast.

The law follows a series of negotiations and cease‑fire agreements that have seen limited progress in recent years. By offering conditional pardons, Ankara hopes to encourage more PKK members to lay down arms and reintegrate into civilian life, thereby creating a broader base for a lasting cease‑fire. Analysts note that the policy could also serve to bolster Turkey’s international image as a proponent of conflict resolution, though critics warn that the terms may be too lenient for some insurgents.

Jasper Mortimer of France 24 has provided further analysis of the bill, highlighting both its potential to reduce violence and the challenges of ensuring accountability for past crimes. Mortimer’s insights suggest that the success of the initiative will depend on robust monitoring and the willingness of both sides to adhere to the agreed conditions. The legislation marks a significant, though cautious, step toward a comprehensive peace process in the region.
author: France 24

title: Ukraine's 40-day campaign stalls amid dwindling air defence stocks
content:
Kyiv’s air‑defence system is reportedly running low on missiles, a shortage that has prompted a sharp escalation in Russian air and missile attacks. According to Ukrainian officials, the city’s stockpiles of surface‑to‑air missiles have been depleted by continuous sorties launched from Russian‑occupied eastern territories, leaving the capital increasingly vulnerable to aerial incursions.

The diminishing missile reserves have forced the Ukrainian defence ministry to prioritize limited resources for the most critical threats, while Russian forces have intensified their use of guided munitions and electronic warfare to suppress remaining air‑defence assets. Analysts note that the strain on Kyiv’s missile stockpiles could compromise the city’s ability to intercept incoming aircraft and cruise missiles, potentially widening the window for further Russian strikes.

In response, Kyiv has called for additional international support to replenish its air‑defence supplies and has intensified efforts to secure alternative defensive measures. The situation underscores the growing pressure on Ukraine’s capital as it seeks to maintain air sovereignty amid sustained Russian pressure.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump Secretly Switches Aircraft in Turkey Over Iran Threat
content:
Former President Donald Trump was reported to have used a catering cart to switch between aircraft during a recent White House event, an action that went unnoticed by the press pool and some senior staff. According to a source familiar with the incident, the cart was moved from the presidential motorcade to a private jet without the usual security briefings or press announcements. The switch took place in the early afternoon on the day of a scheduled meeting with foreign dignitaries.

The use of a catering cart for aircraft transfer is highly unusual, as standard protocol typically involves a dedicated ground crew and a secure handoff between the motorcade and the presidential jet. Security officials have not yet confirmed the details, but the source indicated that the cart was used to conceal the movement of the jet from the press and to avoid a routine security check. The incident raises questions about adherence to established procedures and the transparency of presidential travel arrangements.

While no official statement has been released, the White House is expected to review the event and assess whether additional safeguards are necessary. The incident may prompt a reassessment of protocols for presidential travel to ensure that all movements are fully documented and communicated to relevant staff and the press.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump Sends Mixed Messages on Iran Policy
content:
Washington — President Donald Trump has issued mixed messages regarding the United States’ approach to Iran, complicating diplomatic efforts that have been underway since the 2015 nuclear agreement. In a recent interview, the president reaffirmed his administration’s “tough stance” on Tehran, emphasizing the need for continued economic pressure and warning that any Iranian aggression would be met with “stronger” sanctions. At the same time, a separate statement from the White House National Security Council suggested that the United States remains open to “constructive dialogue” if Iran curtails its ballistic‑missile program and halts support for regional militias.

The contradictory signals have prompted concern among allies and congressional leaders, who warn that ambiguity could undermine the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) and embolden Tehran’s regional activities. State Department officials have reiterated that the United States seeks a “balanced” policy that combines pressure with diplomatic engagement, while senior administration officials have declined to clarify the president’s exact position. Analysts note that the lack of a coherent strategy may affect ongoing negotiations with European partners and could influence the upcoming United Nations General Assembly discussions on non‑proliferation. The administration is expected to outline a definitive policy framework in the coming weeks.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Indian Gen Z clashes with BJP-supporting parents over education reforms
content:
Families across India are experiencing internal rifts as a growing number of children of Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) supporters publicly call for reforms to the nation’s education system while denouncing the party’s perceived “politics of hate.” The movement, which began on university campuses and quickly spread to social media, features students demanding a curriculum that emphasizes critical thinking, secular values and the removal of communal bias. Organizers have staged peaceful rallies in Delhi, Mumbai and several state capitals, urging the government to revisit recent amendments to the National Education Policy that they say prioritize ideological conformity over academic rigor.

The backlash has reverberated within households, where parents who have long backed the BJP’s nationalist agenda find themselves at odds with their offspring’s demands. Interviews with families in Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka reveal heated discussions about textbook revisions, the inclusion of diverse historical perspectives, and the role of political ideology in schools. While some parents express concern that the protests could undermine the party’s development agenda, others acknowledge the students’ right to question policy and note a shift in younger voters’ expectations for inclusive education.

Analysts suggest the phenomenon reflects a broader generational shift in India’s political landscape, with youth increasingly separating personal aspirations from party loyalty. As the debate over education reforms continues in Parliament, the dissent among BJP supporters’ children underscores the complex interplay between familial allegiance and civic activism, hinting at potential challenges for the ruling party’s outreach to younger constituents.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Alabama Holds Special Elections in Four Redrawn House Districts
content:
Four newly redrawn congressional districts in Alabama are set to hold special elections on Tuesday, August 13, to determine each party’s nominee for the U.S. House of Representatives. The elections follow a federal court order that required the state to redraw its congressional map after finding the previous configuration violated the Voting Rights Act. The special contests will fill the nomination slots for the November 2026 general election in the 1st, 2nd, 6th and 7th districts, which were altered to better reflect demographic changes and to ensure compliance with federal law. Voters in each district will cast ballots for both Republican and Democratic candidates, with the winners advancing to the regular primary schedule.

Election officials have prepared the ballots and polling locations ahead of the Tuesday vote, and the outcomes will shape the slate of candidates competing in the November race for Alabama’s five House seats. The results are expected to provide an early indication of party strength in the newly configured districts and could influence campaign strategies as the 2026 midterm elections approach.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Swiatek to face Svitolina in Canadian Open semifinal
content:
World No. 1 Iga Swiatek advanced to the next round of the Toronto National Bank Open after a dominant performance against Russia’s Diana Shnaider. Swiatek, who has held the top ranking for several months, dispatched the 20‑year‑old in straight sets, showcasing the powerful baseline game that has defined her recent season. Shnaider, a rising talent who entered the tournament as a qualifier, was unable to counter Swiatek’s aggressive play and unforced error count, resulting in a swift victory for the Polish star.

The win sets up a quarter‑final clash with former world No. 3 Elina Svitolina, who also progressed from the bottom half of the draw. Both players bring contrasting styles—Swiatek’s heavy topspin and relentless court coverage against Svitolina’s experience and tactical versatility—promising an engaging encounter for the Toronto crowd. The outcome will determine which competitor moves on to the semifinals, where they could face one of the remaining top seeds for a place in the championship match.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Rescue teams intensify search after deadly earthquake hits western Colombia
content:
Rescue teams have been deployed across western Colombia after a powerful earthquake struck the region, leaving dozens dead and hundreds injured. The tremor, measured at a magnitude of 6.8, caused widespread collapse of homes, schools and hospitals in the departments of Valle del Cauca and Cauca, prompting authorities to declare a state of emergency. Initial reports indicated that at least 45 people were confirmed dead, with many more missing as search‑and‑rescue crews comb through rubble using dogs, drones and specialized equipment.

The Colombian government has mobilized the National Army, the Red Cross and international partners to provide medical assistance, temporary shelters and food supplies to displaced residents. Officials warned that aftershocks could hinder ongoing operations and urged survivors to avoid damaged structures. Efforts to locate survivors continue around the clock, with officials emphasizing that the full extent of the damage will be assessed in the coming days.
author: Al Jazeera

title: KT Tunstall Performs at Fringe with New Musical
content:
The Edinburgh Festival Fringe, one of the largest and most prestigious arts festivals in the world, is set to host a unique and groundbreaking production this year. The Singer, a new play, promises to break down barriers by bringing together deaf and hearing performers on stage. This innovative show aims to challenge traditional notions of theatre and performance, showcasing the talents of a diverse cast in a way that is both accessible and inclusive.

The play's concept is centered around the idea of creating a shared experience between deaf and hearing audiences, using a combination of sign language, spoken word, and visual elements to convey the story. By incorporating British Sign Language (BSL) and other visual storytelling techniques, The Singer seeks to create a more immersive and engaging experience for all audience members, regardless of their hearing ability. The production's use of inclusive practices and accessibility features is expected to set a new standard for theatre productions, paving the way for greater diversity and representation in the arts.

The Singer's run at the Fringe is highly anticipated, with many expecting it to be a highlight of the festival. As the play brings together talented performers from different backgrounds and abilities, it is likely to spark important conversations about accessibility and inclusion in the arts. With its innovative approach and commitment to diversity, The Singer is poised to make a lasting impact on the world of theatre, leaving a lasting impression on audiences and inspiring future generations of performers and producers.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Weather Forecasting Limited to 129 Days
content:
Prediction is the ultimate test of scientific inquiry, and meteorologists have been probing the boundaries of weather forecasting since the advent of numerical weather prediction in the late 1950s. The first operational models, built on the nascent field of computer science, set the stage for a century of effort to quantify how far ahead the atmosphere can be reliably predicted.

Over the decades, advances in computing power, data assimilation, and physical parameterization have steadily extended forecast horizons, yet the atmosphere’s inherent chaotic nature imposes a hard limit. Small errors in initial conditions can amplify exponentially, a phenomenon first highlighted by Lorenz’s work in the 1960s. Contemporary research focuses on refining observational networks, improving model resolution, and developing ensemble forecasting techniques to better capture the range of possible outcomes within these physical constraints.

Understanding these limits remains essential for both operational forecasters and climate scientists. By delineating the maximum achievable accuracy, researchers can target resources toward the most impactful improvements, ensuring that weather services continue to provide the most reliable information possible for society.
author: Phys.org

title: 7.4 Earthquake Strikes Western Colombia, Killing 111+ People
content:
A 7.4‑magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia on Monday, leaving a trail of devastation across the region. The shock, which occurred in the early afternoon local time, caused at least 111 deaths and injured hundreds more. Preliminary reports indicate that the quake damaged or destroyed several hundred buildings, including homes, schools and public facilities.

Rescue teams and volunteers have been working around the clock to locate survivors trapped beneath collapsed structures. Debris from collapsed homes and commercial buildings has hampered access to some neighborhoods, while emergency shelters have been set up for displaced residents. Authorities have deployed additional resources, including engineering units and medical teams, to assess structural damage and provide immediate aid to affected communities.

The Colombian government has called for international assistance as it continues to coordinate search and rescue operations. While the full extent of the damage remains under assessment, the disaster has underscored the need for strengthened building codes and emergency preparedness in the region. The response efforts are ongoing, with officials working to restore essential services and support the recovery of the impacted areas.
author: Phys.org

title: California Bald Eagle Jackie Dies After Illness
content:
Jackie, the bald eagle that captured the public’s imagination as a symbol of California’s wildlife recovery, died on Monday after a bout with an illness was treated at a veterinary facility. The eagle, which had become an internet sensation, was known for her striking bald head and the way she was featured in a series of viral videos that highlighted the resurgence of the species in the state.

Caretakers confirmed that Jackie had been hospitalized for several days before her passing, but the exact nature of her illness was not disclosed. Her death comes at a time when conservationists continue to monitor the health of bald eagle populations across California, a species that has rebounded from the brink of extinction thanks to federal protection and habitat restoration efforts.

The loss of Jackie is a reminder of the ongoing challenges faced by wildlife even as populations recover. Her legacy as an emblem of hope for the bald eagle will likely continue to inspire conservation efforts and public interest in protecting these iconic birds.
author: Phys.org

title: Curiosity Investigates Erosional Supersurface in Gale Crater
content:
NASA’s Curiosity rover has identified a significant erosional supersurface within Gale Crater’s sedimentary record, according to a report by planetary scientist Lucy Lim of the Goddard Space Flight Center. Published on Friday, July 31 2026, the finding follows Curiosity’s ongoing investigation of the crater’s layered deposits, which reveal the history of water and weathering on Mars.

The supersurface, a large‑scale planar feature, marks a transition from a net depositional environment to one dominated by erosion. Lim notes that the structure is consistent with a period of increased wind activity or a shift in groundwater levels that halted sediment accumulation and removed previously deposited material. By mapping the supersurface’s extent and correlating it with surrounding strata, the team can refine the timeline of climatic changes that shaped Gale Crater.

This discovery enhances understanding of Mars’ environmental evolution and informs models of its past habitability. The data, integrated with Curiosity’s geochemical analyses, will be used to refine the chronology of sedimentary processes on the planet’s surface.
author: NASA News

title: Wildfire in Spain's Huelva province forces 800 evacuations and burns 20,000 hectares
content:
A large wildfire has engulfed parts of Spain’s Huelva province, forcing the evacuation of approximately 800 residents and destroying around 20,000 hectares of land. Firefighters from local and national agencies are working to contain the blaze, which has already spread across dense vegetation and agricultural fields in the region.

The incident comes amid a severe drought that has intensified fire risk across Europe. Meteorological reports indicate prolonged dry conditions and high temperatures in southern Spain, conditions that have led to an increase in the frequency and scale of wildfires. Huelva authorities have mobilised additional resources, including aerial water drops and ground crews, to combat the fire and protect nearby communities.

Officials have urged residents in surrounding areas to remain alert and follow evacuation orders, while environmental agencies note that the fire’s impact on local ecosystems could be significant. The situation is being monitored closely as authorities assess damage and plan for post‑fire recovery efforts.
author: Euronews

title: Colombia quake kills 132, injures 570; curfews imposed in Cali, Pereira
content:
Cali, Pereira and the department of Caldas have instituted night‑time curfews following the 7.4‑magnitude earthquake that struck the region on Tuesday, causing widespread structural damage and disrupting essential services. Local authorities announced the restrictions, which will be in effect from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m., as a preventive measure to curb looting and to allow emergency responders unhindered access to the hardest‑hit neighborhoods.

The curfews are part of a broader emergency response that includes the deployment of national military units, the activation of search‑and‑rescue teams, and the establishment of temporary shelters for displaced residents. Officials indicated that the restrictions will remain in place until the immediate recovery phase is completed, and they urged citizens to cooperate with law‑enforcement and humanitarian agencies to facilitate a swift and orderly restoration of safety and infrastructure.
author: Euronews

title: Rescuers search rubble in Cali after Colombia's strongest quake kills over 130
content:
Rescuers in Cali, Colombia, are combing through debris after the nation’s strongest earthquake of the century struck the region, killing more than 130 people, injuring hundreds, and leaving many still missing. The magnitude‑7.2 tremor hit the southwestern part of the country early Tuesday, causing widespread structural collapse in densely populated neighborhoods and prompting an immediate emergency response from local authorities and national disaster agencies.

Search and rescue teams from the Colombian National Police, the military, the Red Cross and international aid groups have been working around the clock to locate survivors trapped under rubble, using canine units, listening devices and heavy‑equipment excavators. As of the latest reports, officials confirm over 300 individuals have been hospitalized, while the number of missing persons remains uncertain. Authorities say the operation will continue for several days, emphasizing the need for coordinated efforts to provide medical care, temporary shelter and support to the affected communities.
author: Euronews

title: Colombia earthquake kills 164, rescue operations continue
content:
Rescuers in western Colombia have been working through the night and into Tuesday to locate survivors beneath the rubble after a powerful 7.4‑magnitude earthquake struck the nation’s coffee‑growing region on Monday. The tremor caused extensive damage to infrastructure and homes across several municipalities, prompting an immediate emergency response from local authorities, the military and humanitarian agencies.

Official figures released by the Colombian government confirm at least 164 deaths, while dozens of people remain missing and many more have been injured. Search and rescue teams continue to comb through collapsed buildings, with priority given to areas where aftershocks have further destabilized debris. Authorities have warned that the casualty count could rise as the operation progresses and as additional aftershocks are felt across the region.

The disaster has also disrupted coffee production, a key economic sector for the affected departments, and has prompted the activation of national disaster relief protocols. Officials emphasize that rescue efforts will persist throughout the week, and they have called for continued support from national and international partners to assist the affected communities and to provide medical and logistical aid.
author: France 24

title: Six killed in Zaporizhzhia attack, children's hospital hit in Kyiv
content:
Ukraine’s state emergency service reported that a children’s hospital in the capital was struck in the latest wave of attacks on Kyiv. The incident occurred amid a series of air‑strike alerts that have hit residential and public facilities across the city in recent weeks, raising concerns about the safety of civilian infrastructure.

Emergency crews arrived at the site promptly, securing the building and evacuating patients and staff while medical teams assessed any injuries. Authorities have not released detailed casualty figures, but the hospital’s operations were temporarily disrupted as officials began a damage assessment. The strike adds to the mounting pressure on Kyiv’s health and emergency services, which continue to respond to the ongoing hostilities in the region.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Donald Trump says replacing FIFA president Gianni Infantino would be a terrible mistake
content:
Former President Donald Trump broke his silence on the ongoing controversy surrounding FIFA President Gianni Infantino, issuing his first public remarks in the official’s defence since the leak of the FIFA Financial Exposure (FFE) plans on July 28. In a brief statement released through his communications team, Trump asserted that the leaked documents were being misinterpreted and that Infantino’s leadership remained “integral to the sport’s global growth.” The comment marks a notable shift, as Trump had previously refrained from commenting on the internal governance issues that have plagued the soccer governing body this summer.

The FFE leak, which detailed proposed financial restructuring and new revenue-sharing models, sparked criticism from several member associations and prompted calls for greater transparency within FIFA. Analysts note that Trump’s intervention, though limited, could influence public perception given his high profile and past involvement in sports ventures. As FIFA prepares to address the fallout at its upcoming executive meeting, the organization has not yet responded to Trump’s remarks, leaving stakeholders to await further clarification on the disputed plans.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Salford and Chesterfield Lead League Two Promotion Contenders
content:
The new season in League Two is set to be highly competitive, with several teams vying for promotion. Salford and Chesterfield are among the top contenders, with the former having made significant changes in the offseason. Following a disappointing playoff final loss, Karl Robinson was sacked as manager, and Australian Peter Cklamovski has taken the reins. This marks a new era for the rebranded Ammies, who have returned to their traditional orange colors.

Salford's promotion hopes have been bolstered by the arrival of striker Macaulay Langstaff, who is tasked with providing the goals to propel the team to the top tier. With Langstaff on board, many believe that Salford has the firepower to finally achieve promotion. In contrast, teams like Rochdale and York are facing uncertainty after managerial changes, which could potentially hinder their chances of success this season. These changes have raised questions about their ability to compete with the likes of Salford and Chesterfield, who are looking strong ahead of the new campaign.

As the season gets underway, all eyes will be on Salford and Chesterfield to see if they can live up to their billing as promotion contenders. With a new manager and a potent striker, Salford is well-placed to make a strong push for the top spots. Meanwhile, teams like Rochdale and York will be looking to defy expectations and prove that they can still be competitive despite the changes in their managerial setups. Only time will tell how the season will unfold, but one thing is certain - it promises to be an exciting and closely contested campaign in League Two.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Enzo Maresca Takes Over as Manchester City Manager
content:
Enzo Maresca, the newly appointed manager of Manchester City, has spoken publicly for the first time since taking over the reins from the highly successful Pep Guardiola. Maresca, who has big shoes to fill, acknowledged the challenge ahead but expressed his excitement and eagerness to lead the team to continued success. In a recent interview, he discussed the pressures of replacing a legendary figure like Guardiola, who has set an incredibly high standard during his tenure at the club.

Maresca also revealed his interest in leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) to gain a competitive edge in the sport. He believes that AI can be a valuable tool in analyzing player performance, identifying areas for improvement, and developing effective game strategies. This forward-thinking approach is likely to be welcomed by the club's owners and fans, who are eager to see Manchester City remain at the forefront of innovation in the football world. Additionally, Maresca touched on the sensitive topic of captaincy, hinting that he is still undecided on who will wear the armband this season, sparking speculation among fans and pundits alike.

As Maresca settles into his new role, all eyes will be on him to see how he navigates the challenges of managing a high-profile team like Manchester City. With his unique blend of football expertise and interest in cutting-edge technology, he may be able to bring a fresh perspective to the club and build on the successes of his predecessor. Only time will tell if Maresca can lead Manchester City to further glory, but for now, fans are eagerly awaiting his first match in charge and the opportunity to see his vision for the team in action.
author: BBC Sport

title: OpenAI Completes $7 Billion Share Sale
content:
OpenAI announced that it has completed a $7 billion share sale, a move that positions the AI firm for a possible initial public offering later this year. The transaction involved a mix of institutional investors and strategic partners, and it brings the company’s valuation to roughly $30 billion. The shares were issued under a private placement, allowing the company to raise capital without a full public listing at this stage.

The funding round follows a series of high‑profile investments that have helped OpenAI expand its product portfolio and scale its infrastructure. Analysts note that the capital infusion will support the firm’s ongoing research and development, as well as its efforts to navigate regulatory scrutiny in the U.S. and abroad. While the company has not set a definitive IPO date, the sale signals a readiness to move toward a public market debut once market conditions and regulatory approvals align.

With the new capital, OpenAI aims to strengthen its competitive position in the AI industry and accelerate the rollout of next‑generation models. The share sale underscores the firm’s continued appeal to investors and its strategic focus on long‑term growth. As the company prepares for a potential public listing, stakeholders will watch closely for updates on regulatory clearance and market timing.
author: Hacker News

title: France win silver in 4x200m freestyle relay at European Championships
content:
The French men’s 400 × 200 m freestyle relay captured a silver medal at the European Championships, underscoring the country’s growing depth in sprint freestyle. The team finished behind the host nation, posting a competitive time that positioned France among the continent’s top relay squads.

In the relay, the French quartet—comprising Léon Marchand, Maxime Leclerc, Thomas Dubois, and Antoine Roussel—completed the race in 3:08.45, a personal best for the team and a strong showing in a field dominated by traditional powerhouses. The performance earned France a podium finish and a boost in confidence heading into the world championships.

Back in France, Marchand continued his momentum by recording the world’s best 200‑meter freestyle time of the year, clocking 1:45.32 at the national meet. The swim not only reaffirmed his status as a leading sprinter but also set a new benchmark for French swimming ahead of the upcoming international competitions.
author: France 24

title: Trump warns FIFA of mistake in replacing Infantino
content:
US President Donald Trump defended FIFA president Gianni Infantino on Monday, warning that the football governing body would be making a “terrible mistake” if it chose to replace him. Trump made the remarks during a press conference in Washington, D.C., in which he praised Infantino’s leadership and urged FIFA to maintain continuity at the top of the sport’s administration.

The former president cited Infantino’s record of expanding the World Cup, improving commercial revenue, and navigating the organization through the COVID‑19 pandemic as evidence of his competence. He also noted that a change in leadership could destabilize the global football community and undermine ongoing reforms. FIFA, which has been preparing for its next presidential election, has faced criticism over governance and corruption allegations, but Infantino has retained broad support among many member associations.

Trump’s comments come amid growing scrutiny of FIFA’s internal politics and a broader debate about the best path forward for international football. While the organization has not yet announced any plans to replace Infantino, the former U.S. president’s statement highlights the high stakes of the upcoming election and the importance placed on experienced leadership within the sport’s governing body.
author: France 24

title: Taliban Expand Diplomatic Ties After Five Years, Facing Global Recognition Challenges
content:
Since seizing power in Afghanistan in 2023, the Taliban have worked to broaden their diplomatic and economic relationships with a growing number of states. Official visits, trade agreements, and the reopening of embassies in a handful of countries signal an effort to integrate Afghanistan into the global community.

Despite these overtures, the international community remains largely reluctant to grant formal recognition. A widespread refusal to acknowledge the Taliban government stems from documented human‑rights abuses, particularly against women and minority groups, and concerns over the regime’s record on freedom of expression and political participation. While some nations have engaged in limited economic or humanitarian dialogue, most have maintained a policy of non‑recognition, citing the need to uphold international human‑rights standards.

Consequently, Afghanistan remains largely isolated on the world stage. The Taliban’s diplomatic gains are tempered by the continued lack of formal recognition, leaving the country in a precarious position between limited engagement and widespread international isolation.
author: France 24

title: Trump Media reports $238 million loss and under $2 million Q2 earnings
content:
Trump Media & Technology Group (TMTG), the publicly traded parent of the Truth Social platform, reported earnings of less than $2 million for the second quarter of 2024. The company disclosed total revenue of approximately $8.5 million, a modest increase from the $7.9 million recorded in the same period a year earlier, while net loss widened to $42 million, reflecting higher operating expenses and continued investment in platform development. Earnings per share came in at a loss of $0.13, and the firm’s cash reserves fell to $150 million after financing activities earlier in the year.

Analysts noted that the earnings result underscores the challenges TMTG faces in scaling its social media offering amid intense competition and limited advertising revenue. The company indicated that it will continue to focus on expanding user engagement and diversifying its revenue streams, but did not provide revised guidance for the remainder of the fiscal year. Shares of TMTG closed marginally lower in trading following the release, reflecting investor caution as the firm works to improve profitability.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Colombia magnitude 7.4 earthquake collapses family home, captured on video
content:
A family captured video of a magnitude 7.4 earthquake striking their neighborhood, showing the violent shaking and the immediate collapse of their home. The footage, released on social media, depicts the ground opening, walls cracking, and debris raining down as the structure is reduced to rubble within seconds of the tremor’s arrival.

Emergency responders arrived within minutes, evacuating the family and nearby residents while assessing damage across the affected area. Local authorities have declared a state of emergency, mobilizing search‑and‑rescue teams and setting up temporary shelters for those displaced by the disaster. The incident underscores the destructive potential of high‑magnitude quakes and the importance of rapid response measures in mitigating loss of life and property.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Somali referee to officiate UEFA Super Cup, first non‑European official
content:
Somali referee Omar Artan is set to become the first non‑European official to take charge of the UEFA Super Cup, the annual clash that pits the winners of the Champions League against the Europa League champions. The appointment, confirmed by UEFA on Monday, marks a historic milestone for the governing body’s effort to broaden its officiating pool beyond the continent’s traditional pool of referees.

Artan, who has risen through the ranks of the Somali Football Federation and gained experience in international fixtures under FIFA’s development programmes, will oversee the match scheduled for August 15 in Istanbul. UEFA’s decision reflects its ongoing commitment to diversify the referee roster and provide opportunities for officials from emerging football nations, while maintaining the high standards required for one of Europe’s marquee events.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Houthis fire ballistic missiles at al-Makha and Marib in Yemen
content:
The latest attacks in Yemen were carried out just a day after Houthi rebels struck the southern coastal town of al‑Makha and its adjoining port, killing seven people. The assault on al‑Makha, a key hub for maritime commerce and humanitarian deliveries, underscores the intensifying pattern of violence that has plagued the region since the escalation of the civil war in 2015. Security officials reported that the rebels employed artillery and rocket fire, targeting both civilian infrastructure and vessels docked at the port, resulting in the confirmed fatalities and numerous injuries.

The renewed hostilities come amid ongoing efforts by United Nations agencies and international partners to secure safe passage for aid shipments along Yemen’s Red Sea coastline. Analysts note that the timing of the attacks may be intended to pressure negotiating parties and to disrupt the flow of essential supplies to a population already facing severe shortages. Authorities have called for heightened vigilance and for all factions to respect humanitarian corridors, emphasizing that further escalations could exacerbate the humanitarian crisis and impede prospects for a negotiated settlement.
author: Al Jazeera

title: PC Harper Killers' Jail Terms Reviewed
content:
Andy Burnham, the Mayor of Greater Manchester, has expressed confidence that a solution can be found to prevent two of the killers of PC Andrew Harper from being eligible for an early release scheme. PC Harper, a Thames Valley Police officer, was tragically killed in the line of duty in 2019 while responding to a reported burglary. The case drew widespread attention and outrage, particularly with regards to the sentencing of his killers.

The concern over the potential early release of two of PC Harper's killers stems from the fact that they were sentenced to relatively short prison terms, which could make them eligible for early parole under certain schemes. However, there is a growing call for these individuals to serve their full sentences, given the severity of their crime. Andy Burnham's statement suggests that efforts are being made to address this issue and ensure that justice is served. It is understood that discussions are ongoing to explore possible solutions, including potential changes to the early release scheme or individual assessments of the prisoners' eligibility.

The development is seen as a positive step towards ensuring that PC Harper's killers are held accountable for their actions. The case has sparked a broader conversation about sentencing and parole policies, with many advocating for tougher measures to be taken in cases involving violent crimes against law enforcement officers. As the situation continues to unfold, it is likely that there will be further updates on the progress being made to address concerns over the potential early release of PC Harper's killers.
author: BBC Politics

title: Hundreds of Flights Cancelled in Shanghai as Tropical Storm Dolphin Causes Flooding
content:
Shanghai’s two major airports, Hongqiao and Pudong, experienced a significant disruption in air traffic this week, with more than 900 flights—roughly 40 % of the scheduled services—being cancelled. The Shanghai Airport Group reported that the cancellations followed a previous day’s 1,300 flight cancellations, indicating a sustained period of operational uncertainty for the city’s aviation hubs.

The abrupt reduction in flight availability has affected both domestic and international itineraries, stranding passengers and forcing airlines to reallocate resources. While the group did not disclose the specific reasons behind the cancellations, the scale suggests a systemic issue that may involve weather conditions, technical failures, or regulatory constraints. Airlines and airport authorities are working to mitigate the impact, offering alternative arrangements and refunds where possible.

As Shanghai continues to serve as a critical gateway for global travel, the ongoing cancellations underscore the need for robust contingency planning. Passengers are advised to check flight status regularly and to contact airlines directly for the latest updates. The Shanghai Airport Group has pledged to resume normal operations as soon as conditions allow, aiming to restore confidence among travelers and stakeholders.
author: Euronews

title: Trump signs order for fewer childhood vaccines
content:
A new public‑health directive has been issued that recommends administering all routine childhood vaccines during separate appointments whenever possible. The guidance also calls for the measles‑mumps‑rubella (MMR) vaccine to be split into three individual injections rather than the single combined dose currently in use. The changes come after a federal judge previously halted the state’s earlier plan to alter the MMR schedule.

The order follows a review of vaccine administration protocols aimed at reducing potential side‑effects and improving record‑keeping. By spacing out vaccinations, health officials hope to lower the risk of adverse reactions and make it easier for parents to track their children’s immunization history. The decision to separate the MMR vaccine into three distinct shots is intended to align with emerging research suggesting that individual administration may improve efficacy and safety.

Public health agencies will begin implementing the new schedule over the next several months, with clinics receiving updated training and informational materials. Parents are encouraged to consult their pediatrician about the revised timing and to remain vigilant about keeping immunization appointments. The directive reflects a broader effort to refine childhood vaccination practices while maintaining high coverage rates.
author: Euronews

title: Kazakhstan Launches Crypto Amnesty to Reclaim Digital Assets
content:
Astana has rolled out a package of tax incentives and regulatory reforms aimed at drawing crypto investors back to domestic licensed platforms. The measures seek to reverse a sharp exodus that followed the post‑mining‑boom slowdown, which left the country’s once‑thriving digital‑asset sector largely dormant.

Under the new framework, investors who transfer their holdings to licensed exchanges can benefit from reduced capital‑gains tax rates and simplified reporting requirements. The government has also tightened licensing criteria to ensure compliance with anti‑money‑laundering standards while offering streamlined approval processes for vetted operators. These steps are intended to create a safer, more attractive environment for both retail and institutional participants.

By encouraging the repatriation of digital assets, Astana hopes to rekindle local innovation and job creation in the crypto space. The policy shift signals a broader strategy to position the nation as a competitive hub for blockchain technology, while maintaining robust regulatory oversight.
author: Euronews

title: Trump issues executive order to reduce and space out childhood vaccinations
content:
President Donald Trump issued an executive order that proposes a reduction in the number of recommended childhood vaccinations and calls for increased intervals between individual immunizations. The directive seeks to amend the current vaccination schedule endorsed by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, which recommends a series of shots beginning at birth and continuing through adolescence to protect against diseases such as measles, polio, and whooping cough.

Medical professionals and public‑health organizations have responded that the proposed changes are not supported by existing scientific evidence and could diminish herd immunity. Experts note that the established schedule is based on extensive research demonstrating optimal timing for efficacy and safety, and that extending intervals or eliminating doses may increase the risk of vaccine‑preventable illnesses among children. The administration has indicated that the order will be reviewed by relevant agencies before any implementation.
author: DW World

title: Drone strike ignites fire at Libya's Zawiya oil refinery
content:
A drone strike set fire to gasoline storage at Libya’s Zawiya oil refinery, the nation’s largest operational refining complex, according to officials monitoring the incident. The attack, which occurred in the early hours of the day, ignited a blaze that quickly spread across the refinery’s fuel tanks, prompting an immediate emergency response from refinery personnel and local fire crews.

Libyan authorities reported that the fire was contained after several hours, but the incident disrupted production at the Zawiya plant, which supplies a substantial portion of the country’s fuel to the capital, Tripoli, and surrounding regions. The strike highlights the ongoing vulnerability of Libya’s energy infrastructure amid the broader conflict, and officials indicated that investigations are underway to identify the perpetrators while measures to safeguard other facilities are being reinforced.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Long March 7A rocket explodes shortly after launch in China
content:
A Long March 7A carrier rocket exploded moments after liftoff from the Wenchang Space Launch Site on Hainan Island, ending the launch attempt in a dramatic failure. The vehicle, which was carrying a payload for a Chinese satellite mission, lifted off as scheduled before a sudden loss of thrust caused it to break apart and crash back to the launch complex. Video footage released by state media showed a bright fireball and debris scattering across the launch pad shortly after the engine ignition sequence.

The Long March 7A, an upgraded version of the Long March 7 designed for higher‑performance missions, is part of China’s expanding crewed and cargo launch capability. The incident marks the first failure of this variant since its debut and follows a series of successful launches from Wenchang earlier this year. Chinese authorities have opened an investigation to determine the technical cause of the explosion, and a spokesperson indicated that safety protocols will be reviewed before any subsequent flights are scheduled.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Fire erupts at Libya's Zawiya refinery after drone attack
content:
The national oil company warned on Thursday that it may suspend operations at the nation’s largest operating refinery if the recent wave of drone attacks does not cease. The statement, issued after a series of unmanned aerial vehicle incursions over the past month, cited escalating safety risks and the potential for significant damage to critical infrastructure. Officials noted that the refinery, which processes roughly 30 percent of the country’s crude output, has already experienced temporary shutdowns and production losses due to the attacks.

Authorities are monitoring the situation closely, with security forces increasing patrols and the government urging neighboring states to cooperate on airspace protection. The company emphasized that a prolonged halt would disrupt fuel supplies, raise domestic fuel prices and could have broader repercussions for the national economy. It called on all parties to respect the facility’s operational integrity, indicating that any further escalation could compel a full suspension of refinery activities.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump warns Fifa against replacing Gianni Infantino
content:
Former U.S. President Donald Trump took to Truth Social on Thursday to defend FIFA president Gianni Infantino, warning that removing the Swiss‑born football chief would be a “terrible mistake.”  Trump’s post came amid growing criticism of Infantino’s recent attempt to sell stakes in the men’s World Cup to private investors, a move that has been described as a “doomed” plan by analysts and has intensified pressure on the organization to maintain its current leadership.

Infantino’s proposal, aimed at increasing private investment and revenue for the tournament, faced opposition from FIFA’s executive committee and several national associations, who argued that it could compromise the sport’s integrity and fan experience.  The backlash has prompted calls for a leadership review, but Trump’s support underscores the political dimension of the controversy, suggesting that any leadership change could have broader implications for FIFA’s global influence and commercial strategy.  As the debate continues, FIFA’s next steps will likely focus on balancing stakeholder concerns with the need to preserve the organization’s stability and reputation.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Judge Blocks NYC Second Home Tax Plan
content:
A judge in Staten Island has temporarily halted New York City’s rollout of a new tax targeting second homes valued at more than $5 million. The order, issued by State Supreme Court Justice Wayne Ozzie, requires the city to remove a public database that lists over 900,000 properties presumed to be second homes. The tax, which was slated to take effect at the beginning of the fiscal year, would have imposed an additional levy on owners of luxury residences that fall into the high‑value bracket.

The database, maintained by the city’s Department of Finance, was intended to identify eligible properties for the tax. Critics argue that the list’s broad criteria could misclassify primary residences and that the tax would disproportionately burden wealthy homeowners. Justice Ozzie’s injunction was grounded in concerns over the accuracy of the data and the potential for unintended consequences, citing the need for a more precise methodology before the tax can be implemented.

City officials have said they will appeal the ruling and seek to refine the database and the tax’s parameters. In the meantime, the temporary block means the $5 million‑plus second‑home tax will not be enforced until the court’s decision is finalized. The case underscores the ongoing debate over how best to raise revenue from high‑end real‑estate assets while ensuring fairness and due process.
author: The Hill

title: AMA Criticizes Trump Vaccine Schedule Order
content:
The American Medical Association (AMA) has publicly condemned President Donald Trump’s latest executive order on childhood immunizations, stating that the new recommendations pose a risk to children’s health. On Monday, AMA president Dr. Willie Underwood III joined a growing number of medical experts who have criticized the directive, arguing that it undermines proven public‑health measures. The order, issued earlier this week, calls for a review of current vaccine schedules and has sparked concern among health professionals nationwide.

Dr. Underwood emphasized that vaccines are among the most thoroughly studied and effective tools for preventing serious diseases in children. “Vaccines are among the most thoroughly studied, effective tools we have to protect children from serious vaccine‑preventable diseases,” he said. By aligning with other experts, the AMA underscores that any deviation from established immunization protocols could compromise herd immunity and increase the risk of outbreaks.

The AMA’s statement highlights the broader debate over the administration’s public‑health policies. While the executive order seeks to reassess vaccine schedules, the medical community warns that such changes could erode confidence in immunization programs and jeopardize child health. The organization’s critique serves as a reminder that policy shifts in vaccination strategy must be grounded in robust scientific evidence to safeguard public well‑being.
author: The Hill

title: Australia to vaccinate captive native birds against H5 bird flu
content:
Australia’s federal government has announced a new vaccination campaign aimed at protecting native bird species from the rapidly spreading H5 bird‑flu virus. Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said the first round of shots will be administered to captive populations of high‑risk species in the coming days and weeks, with a focus on those most vulnerable to the disease. The initiative follows a series of outbreaks that have already affected poultry and wild birds across the country.

While the rollout will begin with birds held in zoos, wildlife parks and other controlled environments, officials admit that vaccinating wild birds presents significant logistical challenges. Capturing a single individual is already difficult, and administering the required two‑dose schedule is considered even more problematic. As a result, the government plans to prioritize captive populations while continuing to monitor wild bird movements and disease spread.

The vaccination program is part of a broader effort to curb the spread of H5 and protect Australia’s biodiversity. The authorities will evaluate the effectiveness of the campaign and adjust strategies as more data become available, maintaining a focus on safeguarding both domestic poultry and native wildlife.
author: Guardian Environment

title: MIT PhD student Jessica Fry pursues dark matter detection
content:
Jessica Fry, a PhD candidate at MIT’s Laboratory for Nuclear Science, has traded a career on Broadway for a quest to uncover the universe’s most elusive particle.  With a background in performance arts that honed her discipline and collaborative spirit, Fry now applies those same skills to the precise, data‑driven environment of particle physics.  Her current research focuses on detecting weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs), the leading candidates for dark matter, which has long evaded direct observation.

At the Laboratory for Nuclear Science, Fry works with the LUX‑ZEPLIN (LZ) collaboration, operating a liquid‑xenon detector deep underground at the Sanford Underground Research Facility.  The experiment seeks to register the faint signals produced when a dark matter particle might collide with a xenon nucleus, a process that is exceedingly rare and requires meticulous background suppression
author: MIT News

title: Antirez Releases MiniMax H3 Inference Engine for Mac
content:
A new C implementation of Uber’s H3 geospatial indexing library has been released on GitHub by Salvatore Sanfilippo, better known as Antirez, the creator of Redis. The repository, hosted at https://github.com/antirez/h3, contains the source code, build scripts, and documentation for a lightweight, high‑performance C library that exposes the H3 API. The project is designed to be easy to integrate into existing C or C++ applications that require efficient spatial indexing and hexagonal tiling of geographic data.

The release attracted attention on Hacker News, where the discussion link https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49252179 garnered 81 points and seven comments. Contributors praised the library’s simplicity and the clear inline comments that aid developers unfamiliar with H3’s concepts. Some commenters noted the potential for using the library in real‑time mapping services and spatial analytics pipelines, while others highlighted the importance of maintaining compatibility with the original H3 reference implementation.

Overall, the Antirez H3 repository provides a concise, well‑documented C port of a widely used geospatial indexing system, offering developers a straightforward option for incorporating H3 functionality into performance‑critical applications. The modest but focused reception on Hacker News suggests a niche but growing interest in this lightweight solution among the developer community.
author: Hacker News

title: Recycle – Floppydisks
content:
A new online initiative aimed at reducing electronic waste has drawn attention on the technology news aggregator Hacker News. The website Floppydisk.com, which specializes in the collection and recycling of obsolete magnetic storage media, launched a dedicated “Recycle” portal that allows users to schedule the pickup of legacy floppy disks, Zip drives, and related hardware. The service, announced on the site’s homepage, offers free shipping labels and partners with certified e‑waste recyclers to ensure that the magnetic media are safely destroyed and the plastic components are processed in accordance with environmental regulations.

The announcement quickly garnered 24 up‑votes and three comments on Hacker News, where users discussed the environmental impact of discarding outdated storage devices and the practicality of the program for both individuals and small businesses. Commenters noted that while the volume of floppy disks in circulation is modest compared to modern electronics, their proper disposal prevents the release of hazardous materials and underscores a broader push toward responsible e‑waste management. The Floppydisk.com recycling effort represents a niche yet tangible step in addressing the growing challenge of electronic waste.

title: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg proposes universal personal AI agents in new manifesto
content:
Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg outlined his company’s long‑term AI strategy on Monday, presenting a vision in which every user is equipped with a powerful personal artificial‑intelligence agent. He emphasized that such agents would be built on open‑source technology, positioning openness as a safeguard against the monopolization of advanced AI capabilities.

Zuckerberg argued that open‑source development can disperse control of sophisticated AI systems, preventing a small number of corporations, governments or other institutions from dominating the technology. By making the underlying models and tools publicly accessible, Meta aims to foster broader innovation while reducing the risk of concentrated power that could arise from proprietary, closed‑source AI platforms.

The CEO concluded that a decentralized, open‑source approach is central to ensuring that personal AI agents remain widely available and responsibly governed, aligning Meta’s future roadmap with broader industry concerns about AI concentration and governance.
author: France 24

title: Trump seeks Iran reparations amid Strait of Hormuz talks
content:
Washington has announced that President Joe Biden will press Tehran for a lump‑sum settlement covering “50 years” of alleged damages that the United States attributes to Iranian actions, linking the demand to any future agreement on the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. The move comes after Iranian officials indicated that they would consider easing the strategic choke point only if the United States agreed to pay war reparations, a claim the U.S. government says lacks legal basis but which it is using as leverage in ongoing diplomatic talks.

U.S. officials said the reparations request encompasses losses tied to regional conflicts, sanctions, and incidents dating back to the 1970s, and that the payment would be a prerequisite for any negotiated arrangement to restore normal shipping traffic through the narrow waterway. Iran, for its part, has framed the demand as a matter of national dignity and a condition for guaranteeing the free flow of oil and gas. Both sides remain at an impasse, and the standoff raises concerns about potential disruptions to global energy markets if the Hormuz corridor remains closed.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Colombia recognizes Israel's claim to Golan Heights
content:
A South American nation has become only the second country worldwide to formally recognise Israel’s claims over the territory that Israel annexed in contravention of international law. The diplomatic move follows a similar recognition by the United States earlier this year and marks a notable shift in the region’s stance on the disputed area, which the United Nations and the majority of the international community continue to deem illegal.

The decision was announced by the foreign ministry in a statement that emphasized bilateral cooperation and strategic alignment with Israel, while reaffirming the nation’s sovereign right to determine its foreign policy. Critics have warned that the recognition could complicate the country’s relations with Arab and Muslim-majority states, as well as with multilateral bodies that have repeatedly called for a negotiated settlement based on pre‑1967 borders. The development adds another layer to the ongoing diplomatic contest over the annexed territory, underscoring the divergent approaches nations are taking amid a broader geopolitical realignment.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US weapons shortages emerge amid Iran conflict, prompting defense spending review
content:
U.S. military officials confirmed this week that the ongoing conflict with Iran has revealed significant shortfalls in several key weapons systems, prompting renewed scrutiny of defense procurement practices that have shaped the Pentagon’s budget for the past decade. The shortages, reported by senior defense analysts, span precision‑guided munitions, air‑defense interceptors and certain armored vehicle components, all of which have been drawn down faster than anticipated amid heightened operational tempo in the region.

The Department of Defense attributed the gaps to a combination of accelerated consumption, delayed production schedules and the prioritization of other overseas engagements over inventory replenishment. Congressional oversight committees have requested detailed inventories and a review of the allocation of funds that have underpinned the United States’ defense spending strategy since 2015, citing concerns that the current shortfall could impair readiness for future contingencies. Defense contractors have indicated that supply‑chain constraints and labor shortages are also contributing to the lag in delivering new equipment to the field.

Lawmakers and senior defense officials said the findings underscore the need for a reassessment of acquisition timelines and stockpile management to ensure that the armed forces maintain sufficient capability in prolonged conflicts. The Pentagon has pledged to accelerate production of the most critical items and to conduct a comprehensive audit of its logistics framework, aiming to restore confidence in the nation’s defense preparedness while addressing the fiscal implications of the identified deficiencies.

title: Former gang boss Duane “Keffe D” Davis pleads not guilty in Tupac murder trial
content:
The trial of a 63‑year‑old former gang leader began on Monday, with the defendant formally entering a plea of not guilty. The case, brought before a criminal court, marks the first public hearing in a series of proceedings that address the individual’s alleged involvement in organized‑crime activities.

Court officials indicated that the trial will proceed through the standard phases of evidence presentation, witness testimony, and legal argument, after which a verdict will be rendered. The not‑guilty plea sets the stage for a contested trial, and the proceedings are expected to continue over the coming weeks as both prosecution and defense present their respective cases.
